name: profiles.delete swallows the response envelope — twin of the efforts delete defect (a refused profile delete cannot be surfaced)
description:
## Finding (QA, 2026-11-19 shift 5, found while gating `fcf65219`)

`client/src/api/api.js:913-915`:

```js
async delete(name) {
  await API.del(`/api/profiles/${name}`)
}
```

It `await`s and **returns nothing**, so the caller always receives `undefined` no matter what the backend answered. The connection layer resolves the backend envelope (`{ status_code, message }`) instead of throwing, so the 409/error information is destroyed at the module boundary and the UI has no way to show why a delete was refused.

This is exactly the defect just fixed in `src/api/modules/efforts.js:96-98` (option 2 of `fcf65219`): `delete(name) { return API.delete(effortPath(name)) }`, whose JSDoc now states *"Unlike `profiles.delete` this does **not** swallow the response"* — the divergence is deliberate, and `profiles.delete` is the remaining outlier in that family.

## Not the same as
- `fcf65219` — efforts component/module, fixed in the working tree; this card is the profile twin.
- `d4e3a041` — unit tests for the efforts API module.

## What to do
1. Confirm which callers of `profiles.delete` can receive an error (search `profiles.delete` usages). If a caller asserts on the return value or must show a refusal, make it `return API.del(...)`.
2. Otherwise state the decision explicitly in the JSDoc of `profiles.delete`, the way `efforts.delete` does, so the next reviewer does not re-report it.
3. Do not change both semantics in one commit without saying which convention wins.

## Acceptance criteria
- `api.profiles.delete` either returns the backend envelope, or carries a JSDoc stating the swallow is intentional and why.
- Whatever the choice, a case in `client/tests/` pins it (`node --test`, same style as `effortsApi.test.mjs`).
- No silent behaviour change: any caller that got `undefined` before must still work.

## Proof command
`node --test client/tests/<new or extended>.test.mjs` → exit 0 with the new case counted.

**Blocked in practice:** no `npm`/`node` on PATH in the QA environment, so this proof cannot run today — see `91411767`. Land that first, or the test added here is as unverifiable as the rest.

## Scope
`client/src/api/api.js` (+ one test file). No backend change.
